application.name: ofetch
application.summary: A typed HTTP fetch client library ('ofetch' / '$fetch') that wraps the native Fetch API with smart JSON handling, automatic parsing, retries, timeouts, lifecycle hooks, and normalized error objects. It works in both browser-like runtimes (globalThis.fetch) and Node.js (node-fetch-native polyfill with optional keep-alive agents).
application.purpose: Provide a better, safer developer experience for HTTP requests: auto-serialized JSON bodies, response auto-parsing by content-type, retry on transient HTTP errors, request timeout, base URL/query merging, and rich FetchError reporting.

terminology.meaning: The public fetch-like function returned by createFetch; callable directly, with .raw(), .native(), and .create() variants.
Per-request state object holding request, resolved options, response, and error; passed to hooks.
Normalized error thrown on request failure or 4xx/5xx responses; carries response data, status, request, and options.
User callbacks (onRequest, onRequestError, onResponse, onResponseError) invoked at lifecycle points.
Automatic re-issue of failed requests for retryStatusCodes (408, 409, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504) with configurable retry count and retryDelay.
How the body is parsed: json (via destr/parseResponse), text, blob, arrayBuffer, or stream (SSE/text/event-stream detection).
Methods that can carry a body: PATCH, POST, PUT, DELETE.
Prefix prepended to relative request URLs (via ufo withBase/withQuery).
Node.js HTTP(S) agent connection reuse, enabled via FETCH_KEEP_ALIVE environment variable.
Streaming request bodies (ReadableStream/Node Readable) require duplex='half'.

entityAnnotations.businessMeaning: Core factory: builds a $fetch instance implementing the full request lifecycle — resolve options, onRequest hooks, baseURL/query URL building, JSON/stream body serialization, timeout via AbortController, fetch call, response parsing, onResponse hooks, and error path for 4xx/5xx. Also powers $fetch.create for instances with merged defaults (self-call).
Retry-and-throw logic: decides retries (skipped for user aborts), waits retryDelay, retries via $fetchRaw, otherwise throws a normalized FetchError created by createFetchError.
Builds a FetchError with message '[METHOD] "url": status statusText' and lazy getters exposing request, options, response, data, status, statusCode, statusText, statusMessage.
Merges default and per-request options, headers (via mergeHeaders), and query/params into resolved options.
Combines request headers with default headers into a single Headers instance.
Checks whether an HTTP method carries a body (PATCH/POST/PUT/DELETE); used for body serialization and default retry counts.
Determines whether a request body should be JSON-stringified (excludes FormData, URLSearchParams, binary buffers).
Chooses the response parser (json, text, stream for SSE, blob) from the response Content-Type header.
Invokes one or many user hook callbacks with the fetch context.
Node.js fetch fallback: uses node-fetch-native, optionally wrapping it with HTTP/HTTPS keep-alive agents when FETCH_KEEP_ALIVE is true.
Example demonstrating strongly typed responses: fetches repo metadata from ungh.cc and prints name/stars.
Manual playground script exercising $fetch against httpstat.us/500 to observe error behavior; exits with code 1 on error.
Test helper: aborts an AbortController then fetches with retry, asserting user aborts are not retried and reject with 'aborted'.

applicationFacts: Exports two entry points: src/index.ts (universal/browser: ofetch + $fetch from globalThis) and src/node.ts (Node.js: falls back to node-fetch-native, optional keep-alive agents).
$fetch.raw returns the full FetchResponse with parsed _data; $fetch.native delegates to the underlying native fetch.
$fetch.create produces new instances with merged default options (deep-merged query/params and headers).
JSON responses are parsed with destr by default; users can override via parseResponse or responseType.
Errors are thrown for 4xx/5xx unless ignoreResponseError is set; FetchError exposes response data/status and the original error as cause.
User aborts (AbortError without timeout) are never retried; timeout aborts produce a TimeoutError cause (DOMException.TIMEOUT_ERR).
Empty-body statuses (101, 204, 205, 304) and HEAD requests skip body parsing.
Test suite (vitest) runs against a local h3 app served via listhen, covering retries, timeouts, hooks, body types (JSON, form-urlencoded, FormData, Buffer, streams), and error normalization.
Built with unbuild, emitting both ESM and CJS, with undici as an external dependency for Node >= 18 dispatcher support.
